author: M. O. Marshall
title: JD Lamm named head women's golf coach at Troy University
text:
JD Lamm has been appointed as the new head women’s golf coach at Troy University, Athletic Director Kyle George announced on June 17. Lamm joins the program following a successful tenure at Wingate, where he recently led the men’s team to a national runner-up finish and guided the women’s team to first place in stroke play at the NCAA Division II Women’s Golf Championship.
George said, “I am thrilled to have JD Lamm join the Troy Athletics family as our head women’s golf coach. He is a culture builder with a proven track record of success everywhere that he has been. There is no doubt that JD will continue to raise the standard of our historic women’s golf program.”
Lamm spent five seasons as head coach for both men’s and women’s teams at Wingate, leading both programs through historic achievements over three consecutive years. He was named 2026 NCAA Division II Southeast Region Men’s Golf Coach of the Year after guiding Wingate’s men’s team to its first South Atlantic Conference Championship since 2012 and advancing through regionals before finishing second nationally. The men’s squad posted a 281.90 scoring average, secured five tournament titles, and had six top-three finishes this past season.
On joining Troy, Lamm said, “I am honored and thrilled to be part of the Trojan family. I’d like to thank Kyle George and Dr. Hawkins for their belief in me and for the opportunity to lead this historic program. My goal is to build a culture centered around work ethic, competitiveness, and academic excellence. I believe that the ceiling for this program is extremely high, and I can’t wait to get to work. I’m excited to lead a team that the entire Trojan community can be proud of.” Under his leadership, Wingate’s women’s team made consecutive appearances in match play at nationals; Amely Bochaton won an individual national title by 13 shots—the first in program history—and helped secure both conference and regional championships.
Lamm previously coached at Davis & Elkins College from 2018 after serving on coaching staffs at Pfeiffer University—his alma mater—West Virginia Wesleyan College (where he was named Mountain East Conference Women’s Coach of the Year in 2018), and Old North State Golf Club as assistant professional.
He also served on several committees within collegiate golf organizations during his career.
